page: Microsoft Azure E32ps_v5 is an ARM-based memory-optimized virtual machine powered by 32 physical cores of Ampere Altra Neoverse-N1 processors running at 3.0 GHz. Built on Microsoft Hyper-V, the instance allocates dedicated single-threaded vCPUs without simultaneous multithreading, backed by 64 KB L1 data cache and 1.0 MB L2 cache per core, along with 32 MB of shared L3 cache. Memory capacity totals 208.0 GB, yielding 6.5 GB of RAM per core, and cryptographic tasks benefit from native hardware AES acceleration.

Benchmark results demonstrate consistent mid-tier execution for parallelized workloads. The 32-core configuration achieves 57,228.38 in multi-core stress-ng tests and a multi-core Geekbench score of 13,047.0, supported by an uncached large-block memory read bandwidth of 171.35 GB/sec and write bandwidth of 77.34 GB/sec. Conversely, single-thread performance trails modern x86 alternatives, reflected in a Geekbench single-core score of 1,129.0 and weaker single-threaded bzip3 decompression rates of 8.9 GB/sec.

Because the E32ps_v5 includes no local disk storage, it relies entirely on remote networked volumes for persistent or scratch storage. The Ampere ARM architecture delivers an efficient core-to-memory density profile, lowering operational costs per thread for workloads that scale horizontally across physical cores rather than demanding intense per-thread burst speeds.

The instance is suited for in-memory databases, Redis caching layers, web serving tiers, and distributed data processing. It recorded 42.33 million Redis SET operations per second and 32.76 GB/sec in static web throughput, while proving ill-suited for large language model inference, where 70B parameter throughput falls to 2.45 tokens per second.
description: Microsoft Azure E32ps_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine featuring 32 dedicated Ampere Neoverse-N1 ARM64 physical cores operating at 3.0 GHz and 208.0 GB of system memory. Operating without simultaneous multithreading, it delivers a high memory-to-core ratio of 6.5 GB per vCPU alongside 171.35 GB/sec in uncached read bandwidth. Benchmark testing indicates stable multi-core throughput, logging 57,228.38 in stress-ng and 42.33 million Redis SET operations per second, though single-core performance remains modest at 1,129.0 in Geekbench. The instance contains no bundled local storage and includes no discrete graphics hardware, requiring external managed block storage. With cost-effective multi-threaded scaling on ARM silicon, the E32ps_v5 is best suited for memory-intensive caching layers, in-memory databases, application backends, and containerized microservice architectures.
